sink: caller string value is embedded, single-quoted, into a KEY='value' line of a hand-built Horizons batch input file that is POSTed as multipart form data to https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons_file.api
guard: bypassable: the intended escaping `.replace(/'/g, "\'")` is a no-op in JavaScript -- "\'" inside a double-quoted string literal is just the single character "'", so every embedded quote is replaced with itself. A value such as COMMAND="499'\nSTOP_TIME='2030-01-01" closes the quoted field early and injects an extra KEY=VALUE directive line into the batch file sent to JPL.
why: Traced the full hop: args (Record<string, any>, not runtime-validated by any zod schema before this handler runs) -> formattedArgs entries -> broken replace() -> fileContent -> multipart 'input' field -> axios.post to the real JPL Horizons file API. The escaping bug is real and demonstrable from the source alone, but the impact is weak: the sink is a stateless, unauthenticated, read-only public NASA/JPL computation API, so the injected directives only affect the content of that single request's own response -- no confidentiality/integrity/auth impact on the caller or any third party, and callers can already smuggle arbitrary extra KEY=VALUE directives simply by adding extra top-level keys to `arguments` (dispatch performs no schema enforcement at all), which somewhat supersedes this specific bug as an attack path.
contract: "JPL Horizons - Solar system objects ephemeris data (File Input)"
